<translate>
<!--T:1-->
The '''Bestiary''' covers the creatures and NPCs that live across the worlds of DragonMineZ: the animals you hunt for food, the hostile mobs that attack on sight, the enemies you meet in raids, tournaments and world boss fights, and the neutral NPCs you trade with. Each one has its own page with where it spawns, how it behaves and what it drops.
</translate>

{{Config|Entities Config}}
{{Note|title=<translate><!--T:2--> Reading these pages</translate>|<translate><!--T:3--> Health and damage values are the defaults of the server's entity settings. Drops come from each mob's loot table (<code>data/dragonminez/loot_tables/entities/</code>), and a mob without one drops nothing. Counts marked "Looting" grow by 0–1 per level of the Looting enchantment, and meat that "cooks if on fire" drops already cooked when the animal dies while burning.</translate>}}

<translate>
== Wildlife == <!--T:4-->

<!--T:5-->
The animals of the DMZ worlds. Many are hunted for food, but dinosaurs, sabertooth tigers and giant fish are '''predators''' that attack players, villagers and other animals on sight. Only the Giant Turtle and the Namek frogs are harmless.
</translate>

<div class="dmz-cards">
{{Card|Dinosaurs|<translate><!--T:6--> Walking, flying and baby dinosaurs that hunt across Earth's wilds.</translate>}}
{{Card|Sabertooth Tiger|<translate><!--T:7--> An aggressive big cat that stalks forests, savannas and jungles.</translate>}}
{{Card|Giant Fish|<translate><!--T:8--> A huge fish that lunges at anyone swimming in deep water.</translate>}}
{{Card|Giant Turtle|<translate><!--T:9--> A harmless beach dweller that drops Turtle Scales.</translate>}}
{{Card|Namek Frog|<translate><!--T:10--> Planet Namek's native frog, with a rare Ginyu variant.</translate>}}
</div>

<translate>
<!--T:11-->
'''Vanilla animals:''' Planet Namek's waters also hold squid, salmon, cod and other fish, and the Sacred Kai Planet hosts pigs, sheep, chickens, rabbits, horses, donkeys, mooshrooms, fish, axolotls and guardians. They behave as in vanilla Minecraft.
</translate>

<translate>
== Hostile mobs == <!--T:12-->

<!--T:13-->
Hostile mobs attack on sight. DMZ has no separate "Earth" dimension: the Earth mobs live in the vanilla Overworld and target specific vanilla biomes and structures. Other hostiles live on [[Special:MyLanguage/Namek|Planet Namek]], the [[Special:MyLanguage/Sacred Kai Planet|Sacred Kai Planet]], in the Hell of the [[Special:MyLanguage/Otherworld|Otherworld]] and in the [[Special:MyLanguage/Demon Realm|Demon Realm]]. None of them spawn in Peaceful.
</translate>

<div class="dmz-cards">
{{Card|Bandit|<translate><!--T:14--> Outlaws that roam Earth's forests, savannas and jungles.</translate>}}
{{Card|Red Ribbon Army|<translate><!--T:15--> Soldiers and robots that patrol around villages and garrison their tower.</translate>}}
{{Card|Saibamen|<translate><!--T:16--> Plant-grown soldiers that can latch onto you and self-destruct.</translate>}}
{{Card|Frieza Soldier|<translate><!--T:17--> Frieza's army, occupying the plains of Planet Namek.</translate>}}
{{Card|Gete Robot|<translate><!--T:18--> Robots from the Big Gete Star that march on Namekian villages.</translate>}}
{{Card|Mini Buu|<translate><!--T:19--> A tiny flying Majin Buu that fires pink ki blasts.</translate>}}
{{Card|Hell Ogre|<translate><!--T:20--> Red and blue ogres that only hunt Evil-aligned players.</translate>}}
{{Card|Mini Janemba|<translate><!--T:21--> A stampede that charges anyone who lingers too long in Hell.</translate>}}
{{Card|Gomah Soldier|<translate><!--T:22--> King Gomah's soldiers, raiding the demon villages.</translate>}}
</div>

<translate>

<translate>
== NPCs == <!--T:23-->

<!--T:24-->
Neutral and friendly characters you can interact with. Besides trading, several of them have a special role: the Capsule Corp NPCs, Namekian Traders and Time Patrollers sell '''treasure maps''' that lead to DMZ structures and bosses, Namekian Warriors defend their villages, and Demon Realm Villagers sell Medi-Bugs. NPCs have no custom drops.
</translate>

<div class="dmz-cards">
{{Card|Capsule Corp Assistant|<translate><!--T:25--> A villager profession that sells maps to Earth's landmarks.</translate>}}
{{Card|Capsule Corp Namekian|<translate><!--T:26--> Sells maps to the structures of Planet Namek.</translate>}}
{{Card|Namekian Trader|<translate><!--T:27--> General goods and the map to the Big Gete Star.</translate>}}
{{Card|Namekian Warrior|<translate><!--T:28--> Flying defenders of the Namekian villages.</translate>}}
{{Card|Demon Realm Villager|<translate><!--T:29--> Residents of the demon villages; some sell Medi-Bugs.</translate>}}
{{Card|Time Patroller|<translate><!--T:30--> Sells the maps to the Demon Realm world boss lairs.</translate>}}
{{Card|Otherworld Tournament Announcer|<translate><!--T:89--> Hosts the Otherworld Tournament and sends you back to the Grand Kai.</translate>}}
</div>

<translate>
<!--T:31-->
The trainer NPCs ([[Special:MyLanguage/Master Roshi|Master Roshi]], Goku, Piccolo, Korin and the others) are covered on [[Special:MyLanguage/Masters|Masters]].
</translate>

<translate>
=== Treasure maps === <!--T:32-->

<!--T:33-->
Every map trade points at the nearest structure of its kind with a red X. If that structure hasn't been placed in the world yet, the trade shows as '''out of stock''' and turns into a real map once the structure can be located; re-open the trade window to check again.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Quest NPCs === <!--T:34-->

<!--T:35-->
Quest givers are a single data-driven NPC whose model, texture and dialogue depend on the NPC it represents. Right-click one to open its dialogue, where the '''Quests''' option lists the quests it gives: available, in progress, ready to turn in, and locked ones with what's missing. It is the same window as the [[Special:MyLanguage/Masters|masters]] use. Examples in the default world are '''Bulma''' at Vegeta's Pod (story deliveries) and the [[Special:MyLanguage/Hell Ogre|Hell Ogre]] in the Otherworld, who tells you about [[Special:MyLanguage/Janemba|Janemba]] and, once its lair is known, gives you its location.
</translate>

{{See also|Custom Quests|NPC Placement and Alignment}}

<translate>
== How wild enemies spawn == <!--T:36-->

<!--T:37-->
[[Special:MyLanguage/Bandit|Bandits]], the [[Special:MyLanguage/Red Ribbon Army|Red Ribbon Army]] (soldiers and robots), [[Special:MyLanguage/Sabertooth Tiger|Sabertooth Tigers]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Frieza Soldier|Frieza's Soldiers]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Mini Buu|Mini Buus]] are '''wild enemies'''. They have their own spawn category with its own cap of '''14''' (scaled with the loaded area like vanilla mob caps), separate from vanilla monsters, so the two never take each other's spawn slots. Their natural spawns follow these rules:

<!--T:38-->
* '''Out in the open.''' They spawn on the surface under open sky (leaves don't count as cover), day or night, but never where block light from torches, lamps and the like reaches. They don't spawn in caves or under roofs.
* '''Inside their structures.''' Structures that define wild-enemy spawns, such as the [[Special:MyLanguage/Red Ribbon Tower|Red Ribbon Tower]], also spawn them indoors, in dim spots (block light 7 or less).
* They need solid ground and enough free space for their whole body, and never spawn in Peaceful.
* Like monsters, they despawn when no player is around.

<!--T:39-->
Monster spawners and other non-natural spawns skip the light and sky checks; they only need the free space.
</translate>

<translate>
== How DMZ mobs fight == <!--T:40-->

<!--T:41-->
Hostile DMZ mobs use the mod's own combat AI instead of the vanilla melee behaviour: they flank and surround you as a group, call nearby mobs of their kind when one of them is hit, give up on targets they can't reach, and animals flee when badly hurt.

<!--T:42-->
Story-style mobs that spawn naturally ([[Special:MyLanguage/Frieza Soldier|Frieza's Soldiers]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Saibamen|Saibamen]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Gete Robot|Gete Robots]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Gomah Soldier|Gomah's soldiers]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Hell Ogre|Hell's ogres]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Mini Buu|Mini Buu]]) fight on the '''Novice''' AI tier: slow reactions, melee, random combos and the occasional ki attack, with no dashing and no Zanzoken. Some of them also fire ki blasts. The other AI tiers are explained on [[Special:MyLanguage/Sagas|Sagas]].
</translate>

<translate>
== Elsewhere in the wiki == <!--T:43-->

<!--T:44-->
* '''Story characters''' (Raditz, Frieza, Cell, Buu, Baby, [[Special:MyLanguage/Gomah|Gomah]]…) are fought as story quest enemies: see [[Special:MyLanguage/Sagas|Sagas]].
* '''World bosses''' (Janemba, [[Special:MyLanguage/Turles|Turles]], [[Special:MyLanguage/Metal Cooler Core|Metal Cooler Core]], the Tamagamis and Gomah): see [[Special:MyLanguage/World Bosses|World Bosses]]. Their minions are listed above.
* '''Raids''' and '''tournaments''', where you meet the raid enemies and tournament fighters listed above: see [[Special:MyLanguage/Raids|Raids]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Tournaments|Tournaments]].
* '''Masters''', the trainer NPCs: see [[Special:MyLanguage/Masters|Masters]].
</translate>
